newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Pao de Acucar eyes Level Two ADR.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Pao de Acucar eyes Level Two ADR.

text.p: Brazilian supermarket chain Grupo Pao de Acucar, formally known as Companhia Brasileira de Distribuicao, said it plans to launch a Level Two ADR program this year on the New York Stock Exchange.
"We will convert our Level One ADRs into Level Two ADRs," the group's president Abilio Diniz told a news conference.
Diniz said he aims to launch the Level Two ADR program as soon as possible to increase the company's profile to investors.
He added that Pao de Acucar is already in talks with U.S. lawyers in preparation for the program.
Pao de Acucar's stock is already traded over-the-counter in the U.S. as Level One ADRs. A Level Two ADR is a stock listing on a U.S. exchange, with no new stock offered.
The supermarket chain went public in November 1995 with a global offering of 10.2 billion preferred shares, accounting for 14.6 percent of its total capital.
Diniz noted that 70 to 75 percent of the 10.2 billion shares are in hands of foreign investors.
